decisions.reason: The scenario review says the handling process uses which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred, while the scene can still change. select_stage2_subset can rank this capture's DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements and hold the remainder on a deferred vector, but that vector stays with the caller. PalletPoseStamped still carries neither a sent index nor a deferred list, the two early returns publish nothing, and a failed estimate still publishes only the failure diagnostic. The changing-scene sentence does not say the admitted count itself changes because the scene can move, and the scenario states no rule for how many candidates this capture poses. The feasibility review says the return is local to on_pair: after the callback returns, the deferred vector is gone, and the handling process still sees one pose or one failure diagnostic and no source indices. A count of one matches today's winner only with the same comparator and the same first-maximum rule; an unstable sort admits the other tied candidate. The proposal does not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms, and it is not already kept or rejected. It does not put the named split on a result the handling process reads.

The scenario review says sending stage 2 only the pallet select_detection already chooses, and writing that candidate's source index together with the source indices of the other class-matched candidates onto PalletPoseStamped, is both sides of the named split on the pose result the handling process reads. Those indices are the slots extract_detection_candidates already stored, and the message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the roster is this capture. The user named the split; the part not named is that both lists sit on PalletPoseStamped. The same two lists on the failure diagnostic cover the path that publishes no pose, and the scenario states no rule that a failed estimate must still publish PalletPoseStamped. The feasibility review says on_pair already holds the class-matched candidates and already passes the chosen source_index into the estimate, and adding an int32 and an int32[] at the end of PalletPoseStamped.msg is a change in the message this package already generates. EstimatePoseOutcome does not carry the deferred indices, so both publishers have to receive the split from the callback. The geometry_msgs pose on the same path cannot carry the roster, the two early returns stay silent, and the recorder's pose dict does not copy the new fields, so a report row still has no roster; those limits leave the lists on PalletPoseStamped for a successful estimate. The proposal does not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms, and it is not already kept or rejected.

The scenario review says the scenario names a pallet pose and which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred. It states no rule that this capture sends two faces, and no rule that the faces with the largest area_px are the pallets the vehicle handles. A face that was sent through stage 2 and whose estimate fails is absent from the published poses and absent from the deferred marks. The feasibility review says the top two by area, then score, then source index is a new ranking, and the second estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 continues the node rng_ seeded at 0, so its plane depends on how many draws the first face consumed and every later pair on this node is shifted. publish_pose does not copy instance_id, so neither pose is tied to a source index. The recorder stores one pose per input_rgb_stamp and replaces it when a second rich message arrives, and its bbox still comes from detection_selection, which this ranking leaves unused. There is no deferred message: a PalletPoseStamped used as a bare index is stored as a pose, and a WARN diagnostic can overwrite a real failure. The proposal does not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms, and it is not already kept or rejected.
